domain_label: Turlock Independent Health & Wellness Supply Chain, Capex, Labor, Licensing and Operating Model
purpose: A session-bounded method for an independent Turlock Health & Wellness operator (one of the 26 verified independents across Dental, Optometry, Chiropractic, Physical Therapy, independent Gym/Fitness, and Yoga/Wellness) to design and harden an operating model by assigning the business to the insurance-reimbursed clinical engine or the cash/membership wellness engine, profiling its dominant input cost center, mapping the verified regional supplier and buying-group universe, sizing capex by tier, choosing the right labor model (clinical W-2 vs cash 1099/AB-5), clearing the healing-arts licensing and Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal billing-enrollment gates, managing payer reimbursement as the binding clinical constraint, and keeping every revenue/margin figure a labeled benchmark estimate rather than a stated fact for any named business.
assumptions: no per-business operational dataset is supplied; channel, capex, labor, and cost-share weights are reasoned heuristic priors keyed to the health_wellness deep-dive, not invoices or filings

the operator runs one of the 26 verified independent Turlock Health & Wellness formats profiled in the deep-dive (dental office, optometry practice, chiropractic clinic, PT clinic, independent gym/fitness studio, or yoga/wellness studio)
the geography is Turlock / Stanislaus County in the Modesto MSA in 2026, a high-Medi-Cal county ~15 minutes from Modesto hospital systems that leak higher-acuity demand

supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts, unless the deep-dive cites the relationship (only Mas Vida's bilingual positioning and the family-dynasty practice names are structurally documented)

per-business revenue, margin, payer mix, lease rate, and staffing are never asserted; any dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate (industry benchmark x observable size signal x Central-Valley haircut) tagged [ESTIMATE] with method, source, and confidence
the operator holds or is obtaining the required California healing-arts board licensure and, for clinical billing, the separate Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal or payer enrollment
exclusions: per-business revenue, profit, payer mix, or lease actuals stated as fact (only labeled benchmark estimates and cited public fee/benchmark figures are used)
clinical care protocols, treatment design, and patient-facing service quality (covered by other sector KBs)
site selection, lease negotiation, and the buildout financing decision beyond the capex tier and lease-vs-buy node
marketing, demand forecasting, and saturation/white-space strategy (covered by the market-saturation KB)
detailed wage-band setting and recruiting beyond the clinical-W-2-vs-cash-1099 labor-model choice
the competitive saturation read (businesses per 10k) and go/no-go entry verdict, which belong to the market KB
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for Turlock/Stanislaus County Health & Wellness operations work units, grounded in the health_wellness sector deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md sec 3-4, businesses.json, count=26): its named supplier universe (Henry Schein/Patterson/Benco, Glidewell, EssilorLuxottica/ABB Optical, Vision Source/PECAA/IDOC/EPON, ScripHessco/MeyerDC, MeyerPT/Performance Health/BTE, Life Fitness/Precor/Technogym/Rogue, Mindbody/Mariana Tek/WellnessLiving), its per-sub-category input cost centers and capex tiers, its published cost-structure benchmarks, and its licensing/Denti-Cal/AB-5 gate facts; no supplied operational dataset
source_citation: Turlock Health & Wellness Sector Deep-Dive (FACTORY/turlock_business/analysis/health_wellness/DEEPDIVE.md sec 3-4, businesses.json count=26); dental distributors Henry Schein/Patterson/Benco and lab Glidewell; EssilorLuxottica and ABB Optical with buying groups Vision Source/PECAA/IDOC/EPON; chiropractic ScripHessco/MeyerDC and EHR ChiroTouch/ClinicMind; PT distributors MeyerPT/Performance Health(TheraBand)/BTE and WebPT; fitness OEMs Life Fitness/Precor/Technogym/Rogue; yoga/studio software Mindbody/Mariana Tek/WellnessLiving; California DCA boards (Chiropractic Examiners 24 CE hrs, Dental Board, Board of Optometry $275 app/$500 biennial, PT Board $300/$150/$200); Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal provider enrollment; AB-5/Dynamex ABC test; 2026 Medicare conversion factor ~$33.40; 2024 Medi-Cal unwinding ~17,000 county enrollees; industry cost-structure benchmarks cited in the deep-dive; heuristic priors where no operational dataset is supplied

glossary.definition: The insurance-reimbursed half of the sector (Dental, Optometry, Physical Therapy, and the personal-injury slice of Chiropractic) whose revenue is gated by payer contracts - Delta Dental, VSP/EyeMed, Medicare, commercial PPOs, and heavily Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal - and which runs a physical-goods supply chain of consumables, restorations, frames, lenses, and modalities.

The cash/membership half of the sector (independent gyms, yoga, barre, and the cash-maintenance slice of Chiropractic) whose revenue is membership, class-pack, or cash-pay with almost no payer billing, and whose 'supply chain' is durable capital equipment plus facility plus instructor labor rather than perishable consumables.

A group purchasing organization or optical buying group (dental GPOs; Vision Source, PECAA, IDOC, EPON for optical) that aggregates small independents' volume to pull COGS toward the low end of the band against the dental big-three and EssilorLuxottica/ABB pricing power; a clinical-engine cost lever with no analog on the cash engine.

The provider enrollment a clinical office must hold to bill California's low-income public dental/health program, separate from professional licensure; required to bill the Medi-Cal majority that dominates Stanislaus County, reimbursing below commercial PPO with heavier admin, so the enrollment decision is a margin choice as much as a compliance one.

The share of an exam patient's frame/lens/contact purchase an optometry practice retains in-house rather than losing to Costco or online eyewear; the margin engine of the optometry format, because the exam itself is not where the margin sits, and the reason buying-group COGS control matters.

The California worker-classification rule (Dynamex/ABC test) that determines whether a per-class fitness or yoga instructor is a 1099 contractor or a W-2 employee; misclassifying core instructors as 1099 is the structural cash-engine labor risk, since reclassification can retroactively reprice the studio's largest cost line.

The cross-sector ranking of capital build-out intensity the deep-dive documents - dental ~ optometry > PT > chiropractic ~ gym > yoga - from a high-six-figure dental/optical build (chairs, CBCT, phoropter, OCT, edger) down to a yoga studio's flooring, mirrors, sound, and optional heat.

A revenue/margin/market-size figure built as a published industry benchmark times an observable size signal (provider count where inferable, format) times a ~0.80-0.90 Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, explicitly tagged [ESTIMATE] with method, public source, and a confidence word - never a claim of a named business's actual figure.

A business that operates in both engines at once - Elite Physical Therapy & Fitness (PT clinical plus fitness cash) and I Am Yoga Wellness Studio (yoga/wellness plus Pilates/fitness) - and therefore carries two operating models, a clinical supply/DME chain and a cash-engine equipment/capex line, simultaneously.

The margin compression on the clinical engine from Denti-Cal rates below commercial PPO, the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor (~$33.40, net ~-1%), and the 2024 Medi-Cal unwinding (~17,000 county enrollees lost), which the deep-dive identifies as binding clinical margin more than any input cost - dated facts in a moving system.

nodes.definition: Establish the defining structural fact of Turlock's independent Health & Wellness sector: it is not one market but two distinct operating engines that drive every input, supplier, capex, labor, and licensing decision downstream. The insurance-reimbursed clinical engine (Dental's seven offices such as American Family Dentistry and Healthy Smile Dental, Optometry's six practices including Turlock Eyecare since 1950, the three PT clinics, and the personal-injury slice of Chiropractic like Dr. Greg Jones's auto-injury practice) runs on payer contracts and a physical-goods supply chain. The cash/membership wellness engine (Barre Defined, Curl Fitness, Workout Studio by KB, I Am Yoga Wellness Studio, plus the maintenance-cash slice of chiropractors like Atkinson and Beech) runs on memberships, class packs, capital equipment, and instructor labor with almost no payer billing. Two businesses straddle both engines (Elite Physical Therapy & Fitness, I Am Yoga), so the operating model for them is explicitly bi-modal.

included: which sub-categories sit in each engine

pros.claim: Naming the two engines up front routes every later decision to the right binding constraint (reimbursement vs utilization)
pros.example: recognizing a yoga studio is a cash-engine business stops the operator from chasing payer contracts it will never bill

cons.claim: The clean two-engine split understates the two straddle businesses that carry both a clinical supply chain and a gym capex line
cons.example: treating Elite PT & Fitness as pure clinical and missing its gym-equipment capex

failure_modes: applying the cash-engine utilization lens to a reimbursement-gated dental office
ignoring the bi-modal straddles and mis-modeling Elite PT & Fitness or I Am Yoga
acceptance_tests: the analysis assigns the operator's sub-category to the clinical or cash engine and flags it if it is one of the two straddles
revisit_triggers: a business adds a second engine (e.g., a clinic adds a cash wellness line)
the sector adds a new sub-category

base.update_signal: a sub-category shifts engine or a new format enters the sector

nodes.definition: Pin down, for the operator's specific Health & Wellness sub-category, the dominant input/cost center and how the remaining inputs rank by spend and risk. For Dental it is consumables (gloves, anesthetic, composites, impression/scan materials) plus lab-fabricated restorations; for Optometry it is optical COGS (frames, finished lenses, contacts) where eyewear capture is the margin engine and the exam is not; for Chiropractic it is owner labor plus rent plus EHR with very low consumable COGS; for Physical Therapy it is licensed-PT labor (~70% of fixed overhead) plus modalities; for independent gyms/fitness it is capital equipment plus lease plus per-class instructor labor at near-zero COGS; for Yoga/Wellness it is rent plus per-class instructor pay with the lowest capex in the sector. This profile is the raw input that bounds every supplier, capex, and labor decision downstream.

included: input ranking by spend and risk
the inputs the operating plan must protect first

pros.claim: Naming the one dominant cost center focuses effort where margin is actually won or lost in each format
pros.example: an optometry practice recognizing eyewear capture (not the exam) as its margin engine prioritizes frame/lens buying-group cost control

cons.claim: Over-fixating on the single biggest input can starve a smaller input with higher stockout or compliance risk
cons.example: a dental office optimizing composite price while letting a sterilization-consumable stockout halt the operatory

failure_modes: importing another sub-category's cost profile so the wrong input is protected
treating labor-dominated formats like PT or yoga as consumable-cost problems
acceptance_tests: the profile names the sub-category's dominant cost center as the deep-dive marks it and ranks at least three more inputs by spend and risk
revisit_triggers: the operator adds a service line that shifts the dominant input
a previously minor input becomes the binding cost or risk

base.update_signal: the sub-category, service mix, or dominant input cost center changes

nodes.definition: Enumerate the realistic supplier universe verified to serve Turlock/Stanislaus County Health & Wellness independents and segment it by sub-category channel: dental distributors (Henry Schein, Patterson, Benco - the big three at ~85% of distributor sales) and labs (Glidewell); optical vendors (EssilorLuxottica for frames/lenses, ABB Optical for contacts) and buying groups (Vision Source, PECAA, IDOC, EPON); chiropractic equipment (ScripHessco, MeyerDC) and EHR (ChiroTouch, ClinicMind); PT/DME distributors (MeyerPT, Performance Health/TheraBand, BTE) and EHR (WebPT); fitness equipment OEMs (Life Fitness, Precor, Technogym, Rogue); and yoga prop/software vendors (Mindbody, Mariana Tek, WellnessLiving). Each link from a specific named Turlock practice to a specific supplier is representative inference unless a cited source states it; the supplier set itself is the verified-to-serve-this-geography universe.

included: the sub-category-segmented supplier and buying-group universe

pros.claim: A pre-mapped supplier universe stops the operator from sourcing through vendors that do not serve the Central Valley
pros.example: knowing ABB Optical serves ~two-thirds of ECPs lets an optometry startup route contacts there rather than cold-calling

cons.claim: A fixed universe can ossify and miss a new entrant or a vendor that recently changed terms
cons.example: overlooking a new GPO that postdates the deep-dive snapshot

failure_modes: treating an inferred supplier-to-business link as a confirmed contract
omitting the buying-group nodes that defend small-independent COGS
acceptance_tests: the universe lists at least six sub-category channel segments with at least one named verified provider each and tags every named-business link as verified or inference
revisit_triggers: a distributor, OEM, or buying group opens, closes, merges, or changes Turlock reach
a buying-group membership becomes available or lapses

base.update_signal: the verified supplier set or its Turlock reach changes

nodes.definition: Establish the California Department of Consumer Affairs healing-arts board licensing footprint that gates any clinical Health & Wellness setup before operations begin, plus the lighter studio gates. The concrete gates are: the Board of Chiropractic Examiners (annual DC renewal, 24 CE hours/yr including 2 hrs Ethics & Law, RHB radiologic registration for X-ray); the Dental Board of California (DDS/RDH licensure, X-ray/CBCT registration, OSHA/Cal-OSHA infection control, biohazard waste); the State Board of Optometry (exam app fee $275, biennial renewal $500, glaucoma/TPA certs expand billable scope); and the Physical Therapy Board of California (app $300, initial license $150, $200 renewal, direct access with limits). Cross-cutting are the City of Turlock business license, professional liability/malpractice, ADA facility compliance, and CSLB governing only the build-out contractor, not the practice.

included: per-board clinical licensure and CE/registration gates

pros.claim: Pricing the licensing gate up front prevents a clinic from building out before it can legally practice or bill
pros.example: an optometry startup budgeting the $275 exam app and $500 biennial renewal plus glaucoma/TPA certs before signing a lease

cons.claim: Treating every board gate as identical over-states the entry cost for a low-gate studio that needs only a city business license
cons.example: a yoga studio assuming a healing-arts board licensure burden it does not face

failure_modes: missing the X-ray/CBCT or RHB radiologic registration separate from base licensure
under-budgeting CE-hour and renewal recurrence
acceptance_tests: the relevant board licensure, CE/registration, and cited fee figures are listed for the operator's sub-category before any build-out or order
revisit_triggers: a board fee schedule or CE requirement changes
the operator adds a scope (e.g., X-ray, TPA) that triggers a new registration

base.update_signal: a board fee, CE, registration, or city-license requirement changes

nodes.definition: Characterize the payer-reimbursement model that is the binding constraint on the clinical engine, distinct from input supply. Revenue is gated by Delta Dental, VSP/EyeMed, Medicare, commercial PPOs, and very heavily in Stanislaus County by Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal, which reimburses well below commercial PPO and carries heavier admin. The county is high-Medi-Cal and lost ~17,000 enrollees in the 2024 unwinding, and the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor (~$33.40, net ~-1% after RVU changes) is a fresh per-visit headwind. The deep-dive's repeated finding is that reimbursement, not input cost, compresses clinical margin, pushing dental and optometry toward PPO/cash share and making payer mix the live moving risk on the clinical side.

included: the payer set and Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal weight
the 2026 Medicare PT cut and 2024 unwinding facts

pros.claim: Framing reimbursement as the binding clinical constraint stops an operator from blaming input cost for a margin a payer mix sets
pros.example: a dental office recognizing Denti-Cal rate compression, not composite price, as its margin driver and shifting toward PPO/cash share

cons.claim: A payer-mix focus can under-weight the real input and capex cost that still bounds the clinical model
cons.example: assuming better payer mix alone fixes margin while a six-figure CBCT capex line is unaddressed

failure_modes: quoting the 2026 Medicare PT cut or 2024 unwinding figures as static rather than moving
applying the clinical reimbursement lens to a cash-engine studio
acceptance_tests: the payer set and the Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal weight are stated with the 2026 Medicare PT and 2024 unwinding figures labeled as dated facts in a moving system
revisit_triggers: a Medicare conversion factor or Denti-Cal rate update
a Medi-Cal enrollment swing in the county

base.update_signal: a reimbursement rate, payer mix, or Medi-Cal enrollment figure changes

nodes.definition: Set up the dental supply chain that anchors Turlock's seven independent offices (American Family Dentistry, Hawkeye Family Dental, Healthy Smile Dental, Melgosa Dental, Turlock Family Dentistry, Turlock Smiles Dentistry, Valley Dental Turlock). Consumables (gloves, anesthetic, composites, impression/scan materials, sterilization) flow near-JIT from the big three distributors (Henry Schein, Patterson, Benco at ~41/34/10% share) above free-ship thresholds (~$200-$300/order), while lab-fabricated crowns/bridges/dentures from labs like Glidewell take 5-15 business days. Overhead runs ~55-65% of collections (70-80% for sub-$750k-collection solos), with lab fees 6-8% and supplies 5-6%, so distributor pricing power is a real margin risk the demand view misses, counterweighted only by GPO/buying-group membership.

included: big-three consumable distribution and JIT thresholds

pros.claim: Matching consumable reorder thresholds and lab lead times to chair volume prevents both stockouts and cash tied in idle inventory
pros.example: a solo office batching orders above the free-ship threshold and pre-scheduling lab cases against its restoration calendar

cons.claim: Leaning on a single big-three distributor without a GPO surrenders pricing power on the consumable line
cons.example: a startup office paying list on the big three with no buying-group discount on supplies

failure_modes: single-sourcing consumables with no second distributor during a shortage
under-planning the 5-15 day lab lead time and stalling restorative cases
acceptance_tests: the consumable distributor(s) and dental lab are named with reorder thresholds and lab lead times matched to chair volume, with a GPO cost-control note
revisit_triggers: a distributor or lab changes pricing, lead time, or availability
the office adds CAD/CAM that shifts lab vs in-house mill

base.update_signal: a dental distributor or lab term changes

nodes.definition: Set up the optical supply chain for Turlock's six independent optometry practices (Avak's, Generations Family, Monte Vista, Plett Family, Turlock Eyecare since 1950, Turlock Family Vision). Frame inventory and finished/edged lenses route through EssilorLuxottica, soft and GP contacts through ABB Optical (~two-thirds of ECPs), with lens jobs cut to Rx in ~3-7 days and contacts drop-shipped. Optical COGS runs ~27-35% of revenue and eyewear capture - not the exam - is the margin engine, so buying-group membership (Vision Source, PECAA, IDOC, EPON) that pulls COGS toward the low end is the structural cost defense against EssilorLuxottica/ABB pricing power and Costco/online eyewear leakage (Warby Parker, 1-800-Contacts).

included: frame/lens/contact vendor routing and lead times

pros.claim: Routing optical COGS through a buying group defends the eyewear margin that actually funds the practice
pros.example: a practice joining Vision Source to pull frame/lens COGS toward the low end of the 27-35% band

cons.claim: Deep frame inventory ties up cash and ages out of fashion if capture rate is mis-forecast
cons.example: an office overstocking premium frames that sit while online eyewear captures the price-shopper

failure_modes: buying frames/lenses at list without a buying group and bleeding the margin engine
carrying frame inventory mismatched to actual capture rate
acceptance_tests: frame, lens, and contact vendors are named with lead times and a buying-group membership routed to defend the 27-35% optical COGS band
revisit_triggers: EssilorLuxottica/ABB or a buying group changes pricing or terms
eyewear capture rate shifts materially

base.update_signal: an optical vendor or buying-group term, or eyewear capture rate, changes

nodes.definition: Set up the chiropractic supply chain for Turlock's six independents, segmented by model: wellness-cash (Atkinson, Beech), affordability-positioned (Crawford), bilingual (Mas Vida), and auto-injury/lien (Dr. Greg Jones). Inputs are durable capex with low consumable burn: adjusting tables ($1k-$5k each) and reconditioned tables from ScripHessco (the largest reconditioned-table distributor) or MeyerDC (est. 1948), e-stim/ultrasound modalities, table paper, supports/braces, resale supplements, and EHR (ChiroTouch, ClinicMind at $300-$800/mo). The auto-injury/PI model adds heavier lien/collections admin and often a digital X-ray ($40k-$80k) that cash-maintenance clinics skip, so the supply and admin footprint forks sharply by chiropractic model.

excluded: the personal-injury lien-billing economics beyond supply
general capex sizing for other formats

pros.claim: Forking the supply plan by chiropractic model right-sizes capex and admin to the clinic's actual revenue model
pros.example: a cash-maintenance clinic skipping the $40k-$80k digital X-ray a PI/auto clinic like Dr. Jones's needs for documentation

cons.claim: Low consumable burn can mask the EHR and liability fixed costs that dominate a near-zero-COGS model
cons.example: a solo DC under-budgeting the $300-$800/mo EHR and malpractice that, not consumables, set the cost floor

failure_modes: buying a PI-grade X-ray for a cash-maintenance model that will never bill it
single-sourcing reconditioned tables with no backup distributor
acceptance_tests: table and modality sourcing plus EHR are named and sized to the clinic's cash-vs-PI model with the X-ray decision explicit
revisit_triggers: the clinic shifts between cash-maintenance and PI/auto models
a table distributor or EHR vendor changes pricing

base.update_signal: the chiropractic model or table/EHR sourcing changes

nodes.definition: Set up the physical-therapy supply and equipment chain for Turlock's three PT clinics (Altruistic PT, Elite PT & Fitness, Tower PT). Inputs are treatment tables, modalities (ultrasound, e-stim), exercise equipment, bands/weights, and low-cost consumables sourced through DME/rehab distributors (MeyerPT, Performance Health/TheraBand, BTE), with EHR/billing on WebPT. Initial equipment runs ~$50k-$150k. Payroll is ~70% of fixed overhead and the binding cost, revenue is ~$75-$150/visit billing 3-4 codes/session, and a treating PT bills roughly 3-4x salary needing ~200-400 visits/month to break even - so the supply chain is durable and light while the real constraint is visit volume against the 2026 Medicare per-visit headwind. Elite PT & Fitness straddles into gym capex as the sector's PT/fitness dual-engine business.

pros.claim: Recognizing PT supply as light and durable while labor and visit volume bind directs effort to referral-driven volume, not input cost
pros.example: a clinic investing in physician-referral relationships rather than over-buying modalities to grow visits

cons.claim: Light supply can lull an operator into ignoring the per-visit margin squeeze the 2026 Medicare cut imposes
cons.example: adding capacity on the assumption inputs are cheap while per-visit reimbursement quietly erodes

failure_modes: over-buying modalities when visit volume, not equipment, is the constraint
missing Elite PT & Fitness's straddle into a separate gym capex line
acceptance_tests: DME/table/modality vendors and EHR are named with the ~$50k-$150k equipment band, and the labor/visit-volume constraint is acknowledged
revisit_triggers: a DME distributor or EHR changes terms
the Medicare per-visit factor or referral pipeline shifts

base.update_signal: a PT supplier term or the per-visit reimbursement factor changes

nodes.definition: Set up the equipment and supply model for Turlock's independent gym/fitness studios (Barre Defined, Curl Fitness, Workout Studio by KB, plus Elite PT & Fitness's fitness side). The 'supply chain' is capital equipment plus facility rather than perishable inventory: racks, cardio machines, free weights, barre/Pilates apparatus, and flooring from OEMs (Life Fitness, Precor, Technogym, Rogue), costing ~$8k-$10k for a small studio to $100k+ for a full commercial floor, often leased to convert capex to opex. COGS is near zero; payroll is the largest line and lease #2, with lease plus equipment ~60-70% of startup cost. The margin lever is utilization (members/sqft, class fill), and these semi-discretionary cash-engine formats survive only as differentiated boutiques against national-chain value-tier competition.

pros.claim: Treating equipment as a leaseable capex anchor and utilization as the lever frees cash and focuses on fill rate
pros.example: a boutique studio leasing its floor to convert capex to opex and chasing class-fill rather than buying outright

cons.claim: Leasing equipment adds ongoing opex that a low-utilization studio cannot cover from thin discretionary demand
cons.example: a studio carrying a lease payment on a floor its class-fill never justifies

failure_modes: buying a full commercial floor when a small-studio kit fit the utilization
competing on price against a national value-tier chain instead of differentiating
acceptance_tests: the equipment OEM and a lease-vs-buy decision are stated with the ~$8k-$100k+ capex band sized to the studio's utilization plan
revisit_triggers: an equipment OEM or lessor changes pricing
utilization (members/sqft, class fill) shifts the capex justification

base.update_signal: a fitness-equipment OEM/lessor term or studio utilization changes

nodes.definition: Set up the lowest-capex supply model in the sector for Turlock's single yoga/wellness studio, I Am Yoga Wellness Studio (Vinyasa, Ashtanga, Hatha, Restorative, Qi Gong, Yoga Sculpt, Pilates), which also straddles the fitness-studio format. Inputs are props (mats, blocks, straps, bolsters), retail apparel, cleaning supplies, and studio fit-out (flooring, mirrors, sound, optional heat) from prop and apparel wholesalers, with class software (Mindbody, Mariana Tek, WellnessLiving) as the real operating backbone. Rent runs ~20-30% of revenue and instructor pay ~$25-$75/class (30%+ of top-line); the broad format menu spreads fixed cost across more class slots, and the binding constraint is demand/utilization on a limited discretionary wallet, not entry capex.

pros.claim: Recognizing yoga's binding constraint as utilization, not capex, directs spend to class software and schedule fill
pros.example: I Am Yoga spreading fixed cost across a broad Vinyasa-to-Pilates menu to lift class slots filled

cons.claim: A broad format menu raises instructor and scheduling complexity that can dilute any single class's fill
cons.example: a thin Qi Gong slot that never fills yet still carries an instructor cost

failure_modes: over-investing in fit-out/props on a demand-ceilinged format
treating low capex as a green light despite the discretionary-wallet demand cap
acceptance_tests: prop/apparel/fit-out sourcing and a class-software platform are named with the rent/instructor cost structure and a utilization-not-capex framing
revisit_triggers: a prop/software vendor changes terms
class utilization or the discretionary-demand base shifts

base.update_signal: a prop/software vendor term or class utilization changes

nodes.definition: Decide how the operator uses buying-group/GPO membership to counter the supplier-concentration pricing power that is the dental and optical margin story. The dental big three (Henry Schein, Patterson, Benco) and the optical duopoly (EssilorLuxottica, ABB) hold strong pricing power over small Turlock independents; the documented counterweight is membership in dental GPOs and optical buying groups (Vision Source, PECAA, IDOC, EPON) that pull COGS toward the low end of the band. Cash/membership formats (gyms, yoga, cash-chiro) avoid this entirely because their supply chain is durable capex bought once with near-zero perishable inventory, so buying-group leverage is a clinical-engine lever, not a universal one.

included: the GPO/buying-group COGS defense for dental and optical
why cash formats do not need it

pros.claim: Joining the right buying group is the single highest-leverage COGS defense for a small clinical independent against distributor pricing power
pros.example: an independent OD using Vision Source/PECAA to approach chain-scale frame and lens pricing

cons.claim: Buying-group membership can carry obligations or volume commitments that a very small practice cannot meet
cons.example: a low-volume office locked into a GPO minimum it cannot hit, eroding the discount it joined for

failure_modes: applying buying-group logic to a cash-engine studio that has no perishable COGS to defend
ignoring GPO membership and surrendering the only COGS lever a small clinical independent has
acceptance_tests: for a clinical operator a specific dental GPO or optical buying group is selected with the COGS-band target; for a cash operator the node is explicitly marked not-applicable
revisit_triggers: a buying group changes terms or a new GPO becomes available
the distributor concentration or a merger shifts pricing power

base.update_signal: a buying-group term or distributor pricing-power shift changes the COGS lever

nodes.definition: Size the capital build-out by sub-category against the deep-dive's capex tiering (high to low: dental ~ optometry > PT > chiropractic ~ gym > yoga). Dental and optometry are the capital-heavy formats - dental chairs/units, digital pano/CBCT X-ray, autoclave, and intraoral scanners run a high six-figure build-out; optometry needs a phoropter, auto-refractor, OCT/fundus camera, edger, and exam lanes. PT runs ~$50k-$150k; chiropractic is adjusting tables ($1k-$5k each) plus optional PI X-ray ($40k-$80k); independent fitness is ~$8k-$100k+ often leased; yoga is the lowest (flooring, mirrors, sound, optional heat). The capex tier, gated by licensing/registration of any imaging equipment, sets the entry threshold that keeps new-entrant supply orderly.

pros.claim: Sizing capex against the tier prevents over- or under-building the format-defining capital anchor
pros.example: an optometry startup budgeting a phoropter, OCT, and edger as its capital anchor rather than discovering them after lease signing

cons.claim: Treating the tier as fixed can miss a used-equipment or leasing path that changes the real entry threshold
cons.example: a chiropractor buying a new digital X-ray when a reconditioned unit met the PI documentation need

failure_modes: building dental/optometry-tier capex for a low-capex format or vice versa
installing imaging equipment without the X-ray/CBCT/RHB registration
acceptance_tests: the format's capital anchor is identified at its capex tier with a lease-vs-buy decision and any imaging-registration dependency noted
revisit_triggers: a capital item fails or volume outgrows it
an imaging-registration or financing term changes

base.update_signal: a capex tier, capital-anchor price, or imaging-registration requirement changes

nodes.definition: Set up the clinical-engine labor model where W-2 licensed professionals plus support staff are the dominant cost line. Dental runs W-2 DDS/RDH plus hygienists and front-desk/billing, with labor the single largest cost (payroll 25-28% of collections) and some offices adding associate doctors. Optometry runs W-2 ODs plus opticians and support (solo OD income benchmark ~$212k). PT runs W-2 licensed PTs plus aides and billing at 1-2 PTs/clinic with payroll ~70% of fixed overhead. Chiropractic is predominantly owner-operator, often solo or plus one chiropractic assistant and billing, with PI/auto clinics (Dr. Jones) carrying heavier lien admin. The model is licensure-gated, so hiring is bounded by board credentials, not just wage.

included: W-2 licensed-plus-support staffing per clinical format
owner-operator chiropractic and PI lien admin
excluded: the cash-engine instructor/AB-5 model (cash labor node)
wage-band setting covered by another KB

pros.claim: Modeling clinical labor as licensure-gated W-2 staff right-sizes the dominant cost line and the credential pipeline
pros.example: a dental office planning RDH and front-desk billing headcount as 25-28% of collections rather than under-staffing the operatory

cons.claim: A heavy W-2 model with a small provider count concentrates risk on a single licensed professional's availability
cons.example: a solo-OD practice with no associate exposed when its one licensed provider is out

failure_modes: staffing below the licensed-provider count the service volume needs
missing the PI/auto lien-admin staffing the auto-injury chiropractic model requires
acceptance_tests: the clinical labor model names the licensed and support roles with payroll as the dominant cost line for the operator's format
revisit_triggers: a board credential or staffing requirement changes
provider count or service volume shifts the staffing plan

base.update_signal: a clinical staffing, credential, or payroll-share assumption changes

nodes.definition: Set up the cash-engine labor model and resolve the AB-5 worker-classification question that bites exactly the gym/yoga/barre formats. These run owner-operator plus per-class-paid instructors who are frequently 1099, with instructor pay scaling to class volume (~$25-$75/class for yoga, 30%+ of top-line). This is precisely where AB-5/Dynamex (ABC-test) misclassification risk sits: treating a per-class instructor as a 1099 contractor when the ABC test would classify them as a W-2 employee is the structural labor risk the demand view misses. Every studio entrant (Barre Defined, Curl Fitness, Workout Studio by KB, I Am Yoga) must resolve the W-2-vs-1099 instructor question before scaling, because a reclassification can retroactively reprice the largest cash-engine cost line.

pros.claim: Resolving the AB-5 classification before scaling removes the single biggest hidden labor liability on the cash engine
pros.example: a studio running its instructors through the ABC test and structuring W-2 where required before adding class volume

cons.claim: Defaulting every instructor to W-2 to be safe raises payroll cost and rigidity a thin-margin studio may not absorb
cons.example: a small barre studio over-converting occasional substitute instructors to W-2 and inflating its largest cost line

failure_modes: misclassifying core instructors as 1099 and incurring retroactive AB-5 liability
over-converting to W-2 and pricing the studio out of its thin discretionary margin
acceptance_tests: each instructor role is run through the AB-5 ABC test and classified W-2 or 1099 with the reclassification risk acknowledged before scaling
revisit_triggers: an AB-5/Dynamex rule or enforcement update
the studio adds instructors or changes their engagement terms

base.update_signal: an AB-5 rule, enforcement posture, or instructor engagement model changes

nodes.definition: Set up the Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal and commercial payer enrollment that is required to bill and is separate from professional licensure. The Dental Board licenses the DDS/RDH, but Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal provider enrollment is a distinct credential the office must hold to bill the low-income majority that dominates Stanislaus County, and the same separation applies to commercial PPO and vision-plan (VSP/EyeMed) credentialing for optometry and Medicare enrollment for PT. Denti-Cal reimburses well below commercial PPO with heavier admin, so the enrollment decision is a margin choice as much as a compliance one: it caps how many clinical independents can subsist on the Medi-Cal majority and pushes the payer mix toward PPO/cash share.

excluded: the cash-engine formats that do not bill payers

pros.claim: Treating billing enrollment as separate from licensure prevents an office from opening unable to bill its actual patient base
pros.example: a new dental office completing Denti-Cal enrollment before relying on the county's Medi-Cal-skewed demand

cons.claim: Enrolling in low-reimbursement Denti-Cal can lock margin to a rate that heavier PPO/cash mix would beat
cons.example: an office over-weighting Denti-Cal volume and compressing margin below a PPO-leaning competitor

failure_modes: assuming licensure alone permits billing and missing the separate enrollment
over-committing to Denti-Cal volume that compresses margin
acceptance_tests: the required billing enrollments (Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal, commercial PPO, Medicare as applicable) are listed separate from licensure with the payer-mix margin implication noted
revisit_triggers: a Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal enrollment or rate rule changes
the target payer mix shifts

base.update_signal: a billing-enrollment, Denti-Cal rate, or payer-mix requirement changes

nodes.definition: Define the inventory and lead-time model that differs sharply by engine. Dental consumables run near-JIT against free-ship thresholds (~$200-$300/order) while lab cases take 5-15 business days; optical lens jobs cut to Rx in ~3-7 days with contacts drop-shipped; chiropractic and PT equipment is durable capex with low consumable burn; gym, fitness, and yoga carry essentially no perishable inventory, only durable equipment and a small props/retail line. The clinical engine therefore runs an active perishable/lead-time discipline (reorder points, lab calendars, Rx-cut tracking) while the cash engine runs almost none, so the inventory-management effort is concentrated where consumables and fabrication lead times actually exist.

included: JIT thresholds and lab/Rx lead times

pros.claim: Concentrating inventory discipline on the clinical engine where lead times exist avoids over-managing the inventory-light cash engine
pros.example: a dental office running reorder points and a lab calendar while a yoga studio simply restocks props ad hoc

cons.claim: A light cash-engine inventory model can still stock out on a small but essential retail/props or sanitation line
cons.example: a studio running out of cleaning supplies and pausing classes despite carrying no real inventory otherwise

failure_modes: applying clinical JIT discipline to an inventory-light studio and wasting effort
letting a dental lab calendar slip and stalling restorative cases
acceptance_tests: the inventory/lead-time model states reorder thresholds and lab/Rx lead times for clinical inputs and a minimal restock rule for cash-engine inputs
revisit_triggers: a supplier free-ship threshold or lab/Rx lead time changes
a stockout reveals an unmanaged essential line

base.update_signal: a lead-time, free-ship threshold, or stockout pattern changes

nodes.definition: Map the operating cadence and seasonality that differ by engine. The clinical engine (dental, optometry, PT, chiro) runs weekday-daytime plus some early-evening and Saturday blocks, with optometry seeing a Q4/January bump as flex-spending and vision benefits reset and a back-to-school CSU Stanislaus spike (~8,455 undergrad). The cash engine (gyms, yoga, barre) runs the classic early-morning and evening dayparts with a January resolution surge and a summer dip, smoothed by membership cash flow. This cadence drives staffing schedules, class-slot planning, and the timing of supply reorders, so the operating model must align labor and inventory to each engine's daypart and seasonal curve.

included: the optometry Q4/January and CSU back-to-school bumps
the fitness January surge and summer dip

pros.claim: Aligning labor and reorders to each engine's daypart and seasonal curve smooths cost against demand
pros.example: an optometry office staffing up for the Q4 flex-spending and January benefit-reset bump rather than flat-staffing the year

cons.claim: Over-fitting to a seasonal curve can leave a studio under-staffed when the pattern shifts (e.g., a weak January)
cons.example: a fitness studio over-hiring for a resolution surge that a soft year does not deliver

failure_modes: flat-scheduling a strongly seasonal format and mismatching labor to demand
ignoring the CSU calendar's effect on the vision and wellness cohort
acceptance_tests: the operator's daypart and seasonal curve is stated with the labor and reorder timing it drives for the relevant engine
revisit_triggers: a CSU calendar or benefit-reset timing change
a seasonal pattern proves materially different from the prior year

base.update_signal: a daypart, seasonal curve, or CSU-calendar assumption changes

nodes.definition: Model every revenue, margin, and market-size figure as a labeled benchmark estimate and never as a stated fact for any named business, encoding the deep-dive's binding honesty charter. Method: take a published industry benchmark (ADA HPI/dental CPA overhead; optometry GPO/COGS surveys; APTA/WebPT PT economics; boutique-fitness and yoga operating models) times an observable size signal (provider count where inferable, format) times a ~0.80-0.90 Central-Valley reimbursement/cost-of-living haircut, then tag the result [ESTIMATE] with a method, a public source, and a confidence word. Per-business revenue, margin, payer mix, lease rate, and staffing are NOT public, so no dollar figure is asserted for American Family Dentistry, Turlock Eyecare, I Am Yoga, or any named independent; city/county fees and the 2026 Medicare conversion factor are the only [FACT]-tagged figures.

included: the benchmark x size-signal x Valley-haircut method
excluded: asserting any private business's actual revenue or margin

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark method yields a usable planning estimate without ever asserting a private independent's actual figures
pros.example: estimating a single-OD practice's revenue band as benchmark x size signal x Valley haircut, tagged [ESTIMATE] medium-confidence with a source

cons.claim: Benchmark estimates carry real uncertainty and mislead if the [ESTIMATE] label is dropped downstream
cons.example: a planning band later quoted as if it were Turlock Smiles Dentistry's measured revenue

failure_modes: stating a per-business dollar figure as fact instead of a labeled estimate
pairing a high gross band with no thin-net/overhead caveat so high revenue reads as high profit
acceptance_tests: every revenue/margin/market-size figure is derived as benchmark x size signal x Valley haircut, tagged [ESTIMATE] with method, source, and confidence, and no named business is assigned an actual figure
revisit_triggers: a published benchmark updates
actual invoice/CDTFA/county-enrollment data becomes available to replace an estimate

base.update_signal: a benchmark updates or actual cost/revenue data becomes available

nodes.definition: Harden the operating model against the supplier-concentration and reimbursement-squeeze risks the demand view misses, and name a backup per critical input. The dental big three (~85% of distributor sales) and the optical duopoly (EssilorLuxottica/ABB) hold pricing power over small independents, mitigated only by buying groups; the 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor and Denti-Cal rates thin per-unit economics; and AB-5 exposure sits on the 1099-instructor studios. This node makes resilience explicit: a second dental distributor behind the primary, a second contact/lens source, a backup reconditioned-table distributor, a fallback EHR, and a documented response to any distributor merger - resilience bought with a little redundancy cost against the larger cost of a margin shock or a service-stopping outage.

included: a backup source per critical input

pros.claim: A named backup per critical input turns a distributor outage or merger from a margin crisis into a routine substitution
pros.example: a dental office switching to its second distributor when the primary raises prices after a merger

cons.claim: Maintaining backups across every input adds qualification effort and can split volume below a buying group's best-price tier
cons.example: qualifying a second frame vendor used so rarely it never earns the buying-group break

failure_modes: single-sourcing the dominant consumable or optical line with no backup
naming a backup never actually qualified so it fails when called on
acceptance_tests: each critical input has a named backup source and the supplier-concentration and reimbursement-squeeze risks are logged with a response
revisit_triggers: a primary supplier is lost, merges, or raises prices
a reimbursement-rate or buying-group change shifts the concentration risk

base.update_signal: a primary/backup supplier or reimbursement-squeeze status changes

nodes.definition: Assemble the consolidated operating model that turns the scattered input, supplier, capex, labor, licensing, and honesty decisions into one operating system for the specific Health & Wellness independent: the engine assignment, the dominant input and its named primary and backup supplier, the buying-group COGS lever (clinical only), the capex tier and lease-vs-buy, the labor model (clinical W-2 or cash 1099/AB-5-resolved), the licensing and billing-enrollment gates cleared, the inventory/cadence discipline, and the labeled cost estimate per major figure. It is the single artifact an operator works from to launch and run the practice or studio, with every dollar figure carrying its [ESTIMATE] label and every clinical gate cleared before opening.

included: primary/backup per input with the buying-group and capex hooks
excluded: individual upstream node decisions already made

pros.claim: One consolidated model converts a pile of format, supplier, and gate decisions into an executable launch-and-run plan with no orphaned input or uncleared gate
pros.example: a single plan listing the dominant input, its primary/backup, the capex tier, the labor model, and every licensing/billing gate cleared before opening

cons.claim: A fixed plan can ossify and ignore a better mid-stream supplier, buying-group, or capex path if not paired with a review loop
cons.example: sticking to a list distributor when a newly available GPO would beat it on COGS

failure_modes: a plan with an input that has no assigned supplier or backup
a clinical gate (licensure, billing enrollment, imaging registration) left off the plan
acceptance_tests: the model lists every major input with a primary supplier, a backup, a capex/labor/licensing hook, and the labeled-cost estimate, with all clinical gates cleared
revisit_triggers: a supplier, capex, labor, or gate element of the plan changes
the review loop flags a better path

base.update_signal: a supplier, capex, labor, gate, or cost element of the plan changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the operating model alive: a fixed review cadence (e.g., a monthly distributor/buying-group price check plus a quarterly full operating-model review) and the material-change triggers - a reimbursement-rate move (Denti-Cal, the 2026 Medicare PT factor), a distributor merger or price spike, a lost supplier, an AB-5 enforcement update, a license/CE/registration change, a service-line or engine change - that send the operator back through SUBCATEGORY_INPUT_PROFILE and SECTOR_TWO_ENGINES to re-plan. Without this loop the operating model silently drifts out of cost, resilience, and compliance alignment as the moving reimbursement system, supplier concentration, and labor-classification landscape shift.

included: re-entry into the input profile and engine assignment

pros.claim: A scheduled review catches reimbursement, supplier, and compliance drift before it compresses the margin or breaches a gate
pros.example: a quarterly review that spots the 2026 Medicare PT factor eroding per-visit margin and re-runs the PT volume plan

cons.claim: Reviewing too often churns suppliers and re-credentialing more than the margin gain justifies
cons.example: re-tendering distributors monthly so no buying-group loyalty price ever matures

failure_modes: no cadence set so the model is never revisited and drifts
ignoring a material-change trigger and running a now-misaligned or non-compliant model
acceptance_tests: a review cadence and an explicit list of material-change triggers exist, each routing back to SUBCATEGORY_INPUT_PROFILE and SECTOR_TWO_ENGINES
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

the optical vendor/buying-group segment is the routing source

the chiropractic-equipment segment is the routing source
the PT input profile defines the DME/modality/table need
the PT/DME distributor segment is the routing source
the fitness capex-plus-labor profile defines the equipment supply need
the fitness-OEM segment is the routing source
the yoga rent-plus-instructor profile defines the prop/software supply need
the yoga prop/software segment is the routing source
the buying-group nodes in the universe are the COGS-defense lever
the reimbursement squeeze makes the buying-group COGS lever a clinical-margin necessity
the dominant input profile sets the capital anchor to size
imaging-equipment registration gates installing the capital anchor
board credentialing gates the licensed clinical staffing model

licensure is the precondition the separate billing enrollment builds on
the payer model defines which billing enrollments the office must hold

the engine split sets the per-engine inventory discipline level

the supplier universe is what the concentration watch and backups are drawn from
buying-group consolidation is the concentration the backup plan offsets
the reimbursement squeeze is a structural risk the resilience node tracks
the optical supply line is a core input of the consolidated model
the capex tier and lease-vs-buy are core hooks of the consolidated model
the labeled cost estimate is a required hook in the model
the per-input backups are folded into the consolidated model
the review loop watches the consolidated model and triggers re-planning
buying-group volume consolidation competes head-to-head with the supplier diversity resilience needs
edges.resolution_rule: run core volume through the buying group for the break but keep a qualified backup for the dominant input line

edges.why_related: the moving reimbursement rates causally drive the benchmark bands the honest cost estimate must label

conflict_axes.name: reimbursement_constraint_vs_input_cost
conflict_axes.description: On the clinical engine, payer reimbursement (Denti-Cal rates, the 2026 Medicare PT cut) binds margin more than input cost, yet input and capex cost still bound the model - the two compete for the operator's optimization attention.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat reimbursement as the binding clinical constraint but never ignore the COGS/capex floor a buying group and lease-vs-buy still move

conflict_axes.name: buying_group_volume_vs_supplier_diversity
conflict_axes.description: Concentrating COGS through one buying group earns the best price tier but deepens single-channel dependence on the dental big three or optical duopoly, against the resilience of a qualified backup.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run core volume through the buying group for the break but keep a qualified backup distributor for the dominant consumable/optical line

conflict_axes.name: w2_stability_vs_1099_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: On the cash engine, classifying instructors W-2 removes AB-5 liability and adds stability but raises payroll cost and rigidity a thin-margin studio may not absorb, against the flexibility of 1099 engagement.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: run instructors through the ABC test and classify W-2 where it requires, reserving 1099 only for genuinely independent occasional roles

conflict_axes.name: denti_cal_volume_vs_ppo_cash_margin
conflict_axes.description: Enrolling in Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal opens the county's low-income majority but locks margin to a below-PPO rate, against a PPO/cash-leaning mix that protects margin but narrows the addressable base.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: blend enough Denti-Cal volume to use the demand base while protecting margin with a deliberate PPO/cash share

conflict_axes.name: buy_new_capex_vs_lease_or_used
conflict_axes.description: Buying new format-defining capital (CBCT, phoropter, batch of adjusting tables, full gym floor) maximizes capability but ties up cash a thin-margin format needs, against leasing or reconditioned units that convert capex to opex.
poles: lease or buy used to free cash
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy new only where the imaging/clinical capability requires it; lease or recondition where a used unit meets the volume

conflict_axes.name: clinical_supply_discipline_vs_cash_lightness
conflict_axes.description: The clinical engine needs active inventory and lead-time discipline (reorder points, lab calendars, Rx-cut tracking) while the cash engine runs almost none - applying the wrong level wastes effort or risks a stockout.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: concentrate reorder and lead-time discipline on the clinical consumable/fabrication lines and keep a minimal restock rule for cash-engine essentials

conflict_axes.name: eyewear_capture_vs_inventory_cash
conflict_axes.description: Deep frame and lens inventory maximizes eyewear-capture margin but ties up cash and ages out of fashion if capture is mis-forecast, against a lean inventory that protects cash but cedes capture to online/Costco.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size frame inventory to a realistic capture rate defended by buying-group COGS, not to a hoped-for one

conflict_axes.name: differentiation_vs_value_competition
conflict_axes.description: Cash-engine studios survive only as differentiated boutiques because the value tier is owned by national chains; chasing the value/price tier competes head-on with chains the independent cannot out-price.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: differentiate on niche format, community, and experience rather than price against a national value-tier chain

conflict_axes.name: estimate_honesty_vs_decisive_numbers
conflict_axes.description: Honest [ESTIMATE] labeling with method, source, and confidence is less decisive-sounding than a bare dollar figure, but a bare per-business figure violates the honesty charter and misleads planning.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always carry the method, source, confidence, and the thin-net caveat; never assert a named business's actual revenue or margin

edge_cases.description: A dental or optometry office single-sources its consumables/optical line through one big-three distributor or the optical duopoly and a merger or price hike compresses margin overnight
edge_cases.trigger: a distributor merger or unilateral price increase on a single-sourced clinical input
edge_cases.mitigation: qualify a second distributor and join a buying group before single-sourcing, and route the dominant input through the GPO for the break

edge_cases.description: A clinic builds out and licenses but cannot bill its actual patient base because Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal enrollment was treated as part of licensure
edge_cases.trigger: an office opens having cleared board licensure but not the separate Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal provider enrollment
edge_cases.mitigation: complete the separate billing enrollment alongside licensure before relying on the Medi-Cal-skewed county demand

edge_cases.description: A studio classifies its core per-class instructors as 1099 and an AB-5 reclassification retroactively reprices its largest cost line
edge_cases.trigger: an AB-5/Dynamex enforcement action or audit on a 1099-instructor studio
edge_cases.mitigation: run every instructor through the ABC test and structure W-2 where required before scaling class volume

edge_cases.description: The 2026 Medicare PT conversion factor cut quietly erodes per-visit margin while the operator assumes light supply means healthy economics
edge_cases.trigger: the ~$33.40 conversion factor lands and per-visit reimbursement falls
edge_cases.mitigation: drive referral-based visit volume rather than rate, and re-run the break-even visits-per-month against the new factor

edge_cases.description: An optometry practice overstocks premium frames that age out of fashion while online/Costco captures the price-shopper
edge_cases.trigger: frame inventory sized to a hoped-for capture rate the actual mix does not deliver
edge_cases.mitigation: size frame inventory to a realistic buying-group-defended capture rate and lean toward medical eye care differentiation

edge_cases.description: A chiropractor buys a $40k-$80k digital X-ray for a cash-maintenance model that will never bill the imaging a PI/auto clinic needs
edge_cases.trigger: capex sized to a PI/auto model on a cash-maintenance clinic
edge_cases.mitigation: fork the capex by chiropractic model and skip PI-grade imaging on a cash-maintenance clinic

edge_cases.description: Imaging equipment (dental CBCT, chiropractic X-ray) is installed without the separate X-ray/CBCT/RHB radiologic registration
edge_cases.trigger: a clinic operates imaging without its required radiologic-equipment registration
edge_cases.mitigation: clear the X-ray/CBCT/RHB registration as a precondition of installing and operating any imaging capital

edge_cases.description: A per-business revenue or margin figure is stated as a fact for a named independent instead of a labeled benchmark estimate
edge_cases.trigger: a dollar figure is quoted for American Family Dentistry, Turlock Eyecare, I Am Yoga, or any named business without the [ESTIMATE] label
edge_cases.mitigation: derive every figure as benchmark x size signal x Valley haircut, tag it [ESTIMATE] with method, source, and confidence, and pair any high gross with its thin-net caveat

edge_cases.description: A clinical office over-commits to Denti-Cal volume and compresses margin below a PPO/cash-leaning competitor
edge_cases.trigger: a payer mix weighted too heavily to below-PPO Denti-Cal rates
edge_cases.mitigation: blend a deliberate PPO/cash share with Denti-Cal volume rather than subsisting on the low-income majority alone

edge_cases.description: A cash-engine studio competes on price against a national value-tier chain it cannot out-price and bleeds the thin discretionary wallet
edge_cases.trigger: a boutique studio positioning on value rather than differentiation
edge_cases.mitigation: differentiate on niche format, community, and experience rather than competing on the chain-owned value tier

edge_cases.description: The operating model is built once and never revisited while reimbursement, supplier concentration, and AB-5 enforcement all move underneath it
edge_cases.trigger: no review cadence is set after the model launches
edge_cases.mitigation: set the monthly price and quarterly full-model review with explicit material-change triggers routing back to the input profile and engine assignment

workflow.action: Assign the operating engine and profile the dominant input
workflow.description: Place the business in the clinical or cash engine, flag any dual-engine straddle, and name the dominant input cost center
workflow.gate: the engine is assigned and the dominant cost center plus three ranked inputs are named

workflow.action: Map the verified regional supplier and buying-group universe
workflow.description: Enumerate the sub-category supplier and buying-group nodes verified to serve Turlock and tag inference vs verified
workflow.gate: six+ sub-category channel segments each have a named verified provider

workflow.action: Clear the licensing, registration, and billing-enrollment gates
workflow.description: List the board licensure, CE, imaging registration, and (for billing) Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal enrollment with cited fees
workflow.gate: the relevant board licensure, registration, and billing enrollment are documented before build-out

workflow.description: State the payer set, the Medi-Cal/Denti-Cal weight, and the 2026 Medicare PT and 2024 unwinding facts as the binding clinical constraint
workflow.gate: the binding clinical constraint and dated reimbursement facts are stated for the format

workflow.action: Route the sub-category inputs to named suppliers
workflow.description: Route consumables, restorations, frames, lenses, contacts, modalities, equipment, props, and software to named suppliers per format
workflow.gate: every dominant input family is routed to a named or representative supplier

workflow.description: Select a dental GPO or optical buying group for clinical formats, or mark not-applicable for cash formats
workflow.gate: a GPO/buying group is selected for clinical formats or the node is marked not-applicable

workflow.action: Size the capex tier and inventory model
workflow.description: Place the format on the capex tier with a lease-vs-buy decision and set the per-engine inventory/lead-time discipline
workflow.gate: the capital anchor is sized at its tier with a lease-vs-buy and an inventory discipline rule

workflow.action: Choose the labor model and resolve AB-5
workflow.description: Set clinical W-2-plus-support staffing or run cash-engine instructors through the AB-5 ABC test
workflow.gate: the labor model is set with clinical roles or the instructor classification resolved under AB-5

workflow.description: Derive every revenue/margin figure as benchmark x size signal x Valley haircut tagged [ESTIMATE] with method, source, and confidence
workflow.gate: every figure is labeled [ESTIMATE] and no named business is assigned an actual figure

workflow.action: Add supplier backups and concentration watch
workflow.description: Name a backup per critical input and log the distributor-concentration and reimbursement-squeeze risks
workflow.gate: each critical input has a named backup and the concentration/squeeze risks are logged

workflow.action: Assemble the model and set the review loop
workflow.description: Integrate inputs, suppliers, capex, labor, and gates into one model and define the review cadence and triggers
workflow.artifact: consolidated operating model and review schedule
workflow.gate: every major input has a primary, backup, capex/labor/licensing hook, and a review cadence with triggers exists

dominance_rules.rule: Licensure, imaging registration, and billing enrollment dominate any sourcing or build order
dominance_rules.rationale: no clinic can legally practice, image, or bill without its board license, radiologic registration, and Denti-Cal/payer enrollment in place
dominance_rules.trigger: any plan to build out or place a first supplier order on a clinical format
dominance_rules.action: block build-out and sourcing until the licensure, registration, and billing enrollment are cleared

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labeling dominates any revenue or margin figure
dominance_rules.rationale: a per-business dollar number stated as fact violates the deep-dive's binding honesty charter and misleads planning
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure about a named business or its economics
dominance_rules.action: express it only as a labeled benchmark estimate with method, source, confidence, and the thin-net caveat

dominance_rules.rule: A backup for the dominant input dominates buying-group volume consolidation
dominance_rules.rationale: an outage or price shock on the format's main consumable/optical line costs more than the buying-group break earns
dominance_rules.trigger: the dominant input is about to be single-sourced for the buying-group discount
dominance_rules.action: qualify a second source for the dominant input before consolidating the rest

dominance_rules.rule: The engine assignment and input profile dominate generic sourcing defaults
dominance_rules.rationale: the right supplier, capex, and labor model follow from which engine and input dominate, not from a one-size default
dominance_rules.trigger: a sourcing or capex decision made before the engine and dominant input are profiled
dominance_rules.action: assign the engine and profile the dominant input first, then choose suppliers and capex around it

dominance_rules.rule: AB-5 classification resolution dominates scaling a cash-engine studio
dominance_rules.rationale: adding 1099 instructors before resolving the ABC test compounds a retroactive reclassification liability on the largest cost line
dominance_rules.trigger: a studio adds per-class instructors before resolving their classification
dominance_rules.action: run instructors through the ABC test and structure W-2 where required before scaling

dominance_rules.rule: Reimbursement reality dominates an input-cost explanation of clinical margin
dominance_rules.rationale: on the clinical engine payer rates compress margin more than input cost, so chasing COGS while ignoring payer mix misdiagnoses the problem
dominance_rules.trigger: a clinical margin problem is attributed to input cost alone
dominance_rules.action: diagnose the payer mix and reimbursement first, then optimize COGS via the buying group

dominance_rules.rule: Differentiation dominates value-price competition for cash-engine studios
dominance_rules.rationale: the value tier is owned by national chains an independent cannot out-price, so price competition is a losing position
dominance_rules.trigger: a studio is tempted to compete on price against a chain
dominance_rules.action: position on niche format, community, and experience rather than price

dominance_rules.rule: Imaging-registration clearance dominates installing imaging capital
dominance_rules.rationale: operating a CBCT or X-ray without its radiologic registration is a compliance breach that can halt the practice
dominance_rules.trigger: imaging capital is about to be installed or used
dominance_rules.action: clear the X-ray/CBCT/RHB registration before installing or operating imaging equipment

dominance_rules.rule: The review loop dominates impulse supplier or capex switches
dominance_rules.rationale: structured review prevents churning a maturing buying-group relationship over a transient price or rate wiggle
dominance_rules.trigger: a tempting price or rate appears mid-cycle
dominance_rules.action: evaluate it through the review loop and its triggers, not on impulse

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear licensure, imaging registration, and billing enrollment before any build-out or order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building out a clinic that cannot yet legally practice, image, or bill its patient base

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assign the engine and profile the dominant input before choosing suppliers and capex
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a supplier and capex plan around the wrong engine or input and re-sourcing later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify a backup for every critical input before single-sourcing it for a buying-group break
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a margin shock or service-stopping outage with no substitute when the primary distributor fails or merges

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a supplier actually serves the Central Valley before building it into the model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing a model around a distributor or OEM whose terms or reach exclude Stanislaus County

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve the AB-5 instructor classification before adding cash-engine class volume
anti_rework_rules.prevents: scaling on a 1099 base that a later reclassification retroactively reprices on the largest cost line

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every revenue/margin figure [ESTIMATE] with method, source, and confidence when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a planning estimate being quoted downstream as a measured per-business fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Size capex to the format's tier and model before committing capital
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying dental/optometry-tier or PI-grade capital for a format whose volume and model do not need it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Separate Denti-Cal/Medi-Cal enrollment from licensure in the gate checklist
anti_rework_rules.prevents: opening unable to bill the Medi-Cal majority because enrollment was assumed to be part of licensure

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the per-engine inventory and lead-time discipline before the first perishable or lab order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: applying clinical JIT discipline to an inventory-light studio, or letting a dental lab/Rx lead time stall restorative or lens cases

iteration_protocol.trigger: the operator changes sub-category, adds a service line, or a business straddles a second engine
iteration_protocol.action: re-assign the engine, re-profile the dominant input, and re-run the supplier and capex routing

iteration_protocol.trigger: a reimbursement rate moves (Denti-Cal, the 2026 Medicare PT factor) or county Medi-Cal enrollment swings
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the payer model, the benchmark cost estimate, and the affected clinical volume plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a primary distributor or OEM is lost, merges, or raises prices
iteration_protocol.action: activate the backup, re-qualify the buying-group lever, and update the model

iteration_protocol.trigger: an AB-5/Dynamex rule or enforcement update lands
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the instructor ABC test and adjust the cash-engine labor model and cost line

iteration_protocol.trigger: a board fee, CE, imaging-registration, or billing-enrollment requirement changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-clear the licensing and enrollment gate and adjust the build-out and capex plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a buying group becomes available or changes terms, or distributor concentration shifts
iteration_protocol.action: re-optimize the buying-group COGS lever and the backup plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a seasonal or daypart pattern (CSU calendar, Q4 benefit reset, January surge) proves materially different
iteration_protocol.action: re-align labor scheduling and reorder timing to the corrected cadence

iteration_protocol.trigger: the quarterly review cadence proves too frequent or too sparse, or a material-change trigger fires
iteration_protocol.action: tune the cadence and route the change back through the input profile and engine assignment

priority_rationale: Engine assignment, input profiling, supplier-universe mapping, and the licensing/billing gates precede supplier, capex, and labor setup because every operating choice depends on knowing which engine binds the business, its dominant input, the verified vendor set, and the legal preconditions; the per-format supply, buying-group, capex, and labor nodes build the operating mix; payer reimbursement, supplier-concentration resilience, and benchmark honesty harden and honestly cost the model; the consolidated synthesis composes them into a launch-and-run plan; and the review loop comes last because it watches the whole model and routes material changes back to the foundations.
